cosy-lesson.title: "Knowledge isn't free. You have to pay attention.": Richard Feynman

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Knowledge – information, skills, and understanding that you get through learning.

p.em: Example: Reading books is an excellent way to get new knowledge.

cosy-blockquote.p: Attention – listening or looking carefully at someone or something.

p.em: Example: Please pay attention to the teacher when she explains.

cosy-blockquote.p: Free – costing no money; not needing payment.

p.em: Example: This English website has a lot of free exercises.

cosy-blockquote.p: Focus – to give all your attention to one thing.

p.em: Example: I need to focus on my vocabulary list.

cosy-blockquote.p: Remember – to keep in your mind; not forget.

p.em: Example: Do you remember the meaning of the word 'focus'?

cosy-blockquote.p: Learn – to get knowledge or skill in a new subject.

p.em: Example: I want to learn how to speak Spanish.

cosy-blockquote.p: Simple ≠ Complex – easily understood or done; presenting no difficulty ≠ consisting of many different and connected parts.

p.em: Example: The basic idea was wonderfully simple, but the actual execution turned out to be incredibly complex.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mind – the part of a person that thinks, feels, and remembers.

p.em: Example: Meditation helps to calm the busy mind.

cosy-blockquote.p: Share – to tell other people about your ideas or feelings.

p.em: Example: I would like to share my study tips with you.

cosy-blockquote.p: Difficult – hard to do, understand, or deal with; not easy.

p.em: Example: This exercise is too difficult for me.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What is the best way to get knowledge?
★ Complete using inversion: 'Seldom do we discover profound truths without active questioning.'

Why must we pay attention to the teacher?
★ Is it easy for you to pay attention for one hour?

What is the difference between a free course and a paid course?
★ Have you ever done a free online course?

How do you stay focused when you study?
★ Where do you go when you need to focus on your homework?

Why is it hard to remember new words?
★ Do you have a special way to remember vocabulary?

How can adults learn a second language faster?
★ Why do you want to learn English?

Do you prefer simple exercises or complex ones?
★ Do you find English grammar simple or complex?

How does learning change our mind?
★ What is on your mind today?

Why is it good to share our ideas with others?
★ Would you like to share your favorite book with the group?

What makes English spelling so difficult?
★ What is the most difficult part of English for you?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will enable us to digitize and share our experience of knowledge directly. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you personally adapt if knowledge became entirely obsolete in tomorrow's world?

The rapid speed of modern society will eventually make attention an obsolete concept. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be willing to use technology to artificially boost your capacity for attention?

Future educational systems will prioritize the cultivation of free over traditional academic skills. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with free?

As artificial intelligence advances, machines will exhibit a superior capacity for focus compared to humans. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach the value of focus to children?

In the coming decades, remember will become a highly commercialized luxury commodity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where remember is fully managed or monitored by digital algorithms?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our collective ability to practice learn. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where learn is increasingly rare?

Future generations will look back at our current understanding of simple with deep skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about simple to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true mind incredibly difficult to maintain in the future. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees mind at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's capacity for share rather than wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope share will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the mystery of difficult. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your experience of difficult, would you still value it?

ul.li: Incorrect: I want to study more hard → Correct: I want to study harder ((Comparative form of 'hard' is 'harder'))
Incorrect: I am study every day → Correct: I study every day ((Simple present structure))
Incorrect: It depend of your focus → Correct: It depends on your focus ((Depends + on, singular s))
